declared.title: When choice is demotivating: Can one desire too much of a good thing?
declared.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
declared.foundIn: nommée dans la consigne de la session (dossier too-many-choices, 2026-11-22) ; titre relevé sur la recherche Crossref « Iyengar Lepper When choice is demotivating » : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: shoppers (jams) and students (chocolates, essays), field and laboratory; country not given in the abstract (authors in the US)

findings.text: People offered 6 jams, chocolates or essay topics were more likely to buy one or to write the essay than people offered 24 or 30

support.sentence: These experiments, which were conducted in both field and laboratory settings, show that people are more likely to purchase gourmet jams or chocolates or to undertake optional class essay assignments when offered a limited array of 6 choices rather than a more extensive array of 24 or 30 choices.

findings.text: People who chose from the small set were more satisfied afterwards with what they chose (and wrote better essays)

support.sentence: Moreover, participants actually reported greater subsequent satisfaction with their selections and wrote better essays when their original set of options had been limited.

limits: choices of little importance (jams, chocolates, a class essay), not life choices
sample sizes and percentages not given in the abstract
listed in content/contested.json: pooled in scheibehenne-2010-overload, whose mean is virtually zero; failed tests (scheibehenne-2009-moderators)
allegiance: the study that started the choice-overload line; its first author co-signs later work on choice (reutskaja-2022-deprivation)
